questions.question: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only one person sits between R and T when counted from the left of T. Q sits third to the right of P. U sits third to the left of V. Q sits to the immediate right of U. S is not an immediate neighbour of U. How many people sit between S and T when counted from the right of S?
questions.solution:
**Given: **P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

Q sits third to the right of P. U sits third to the left of V. Q sits to the immediate right of U.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5351bacbaba3fd975679c0c61dd0f6f57e35928ab857aeeb53d64462cf3bf80a.png] 

S is not an immediate neighbour of U. Only one person sits between R and T when counted from the left of T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87daf2611ccc289fa58a6b32e76066d83bda79c60558bf125fbd731ef5655c9d.png] 

Thus, Only 3 sit people sit between S and T when counted from the right of S.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**

Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and make the given equation correct.

55 * 126 * 14 * 520 * 30 * 5
questions.solution:
1. ×, ÷, =, –, +

Given equation: 55 * 126 * 14 * 520 * 30 * 5

After replacing the * with the symbols in the option, we get:

55 × 126 ÷ 14 = 520 - 30 + 5

⇒ 55 × 9 = 495

⇒ 495 = 495

2. +, ÷, –, =, ×

Given equation: 55 * 126 * 14 * 520 * 30 * 5

After replacing the * with the symbols in the option, we get:

55 + 126 ÷ 14 - 520 = 30 + 5

⇒ 55 + 9 - 520 = 35

questions.question: Height of 8 boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, and B8 are compared. Height of B3 will be the least or maximum. Height of B4 is more than B6. Height of B8 is less than only 3 boys. Height of B2 is more than B1 but less than B8. Height of B2 is less than B3. B5 and B7 are taller than B8 but shorter than B3. If the height of B4 is less than B1, then which of the following sequence of their heights may be correct?
questions.solution:
The logic followed is:

Height of 8 boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, and B8 are compared.

i) Height of B4 is more than B6.

**B4 > B6 equation i)**

ii) Height of B8 is less than only 3 boys.

iii) Height of B2 is more than B1 but less than B8.

**B8 > B2 > B1 equation ii)**

iv) If the height of B4 is less than B1

**B1 > B4 equation iii)**

v) B5 and B7 are taller than B8 but shorter than B3.

From the equation i) and iii) we can say,

**B6 is the smallest of all. **Thus we can **conclude** from the given **statement i.e the height of B3 will be the least or maximum. As B6 is the smallest, it is only possible B3 is the maximum in height.**

Thus the final arrangement is:

B3 > B5 = B7 > B8 > B2 > B1 > B4 > B6 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**
